proposals.evidence: Platts p. 523 identifies Persian dil “heart”. Dental d is retained here; retroflex ḍil may belong to the different expressive body/lump family and is excluded. Existing Hindi dil “heart” (kannauji[p. 59]) supplies an attested provisional donor. Its locality is the attestation site; the historical lending locality and possible intervening Indo-Aryan language remain unknown. The borrowed edge is saved under the user’s explicit preference to link supported families despite unresolved cross-IA transmission.
